data.body:
Research: Jira-integration deletion semantics (2026-08-10)

Jira itself exposes link deletion as an explicit event and operation, not merely as absence: Cloud webhooks include issuelink_created and issuelink_deleted, and REST deletes a specific issue link by stable linkId. Sources: https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/webhooks/#issue-link-webhooks and https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-issue-links/#api-rest-api-3-issuelink-linkid-delete

A maintained OSS comparison is GitHub's ghas-jira-integration (github/ghas-jira-integration, updated 2026-08-03). It embeds a durable alert association key in managed Jira issues, handles explicit jira:issue_deleted webhooks, and stores a per-repository prior-state map in Jira. Its full reconciliation builds the union of known source alerts and associated Jira issues; it deletes only when an issue is proven associated and the authoritative source listing proves the alert absent. Sources: https://github.com/github/ghas-jira-integration/blob/main/sync.py and https://github.com/github/ghas-jira-integration/blob/main/jiralib.py

Comparison: the proposed peer-confirmed marker follows the same essential rule—absence may delete only something previously proven to be synchronized. That is materially safer than treating any missing inbound link as a deletion. However, a boolean peer-confirmed flag is weaker than the established patterns: it does not retain Jira's linkId, which side created the link, which authoritative snapshot confirmed it, or whether the current read was complete and newer than that confirmation.

Recommended refinement: persist a managed-link record keyed by relation+target containing Jira linkId when available, origin/direction, confirmed baseline or snapshot revision, and last-confirmed time. Delete on an explicit issuelink_deleted event; during polling, infer deletion only from a successful authoritative complete snapshot newer than the confirmation. A partial/paginated/failed/stale response must never become deletion evidence. This retains the ticket's peer-confirmation idea but makes the evidence strong enough for bidirectional reconciliation.
